You claim in your sittings that you would do this and that, but when fighting approaches, you say (to war), ‘turn thou away’ (i.e. flee away).
If one calls you (for help) the call receives no heed. And he who deals hardly with you his heart has no solace.
The excuses are amiss like that of debtor unwilling to pay. The ignoble cannot ward off oppression.
Right cannot be achieved without effort.
Which is the house besides this one to protect? And with which leader (Imām) would you go for fighting after me?
ai.seo_question: What is the critique of hypocrisy in Nahj al-Balagha regarding speech versus action?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) delivers this critique during the period of the 'Siffin' conflict, exposing the political opportunism of those who claimed allegiance to him yet sought to avoid the actual cost of jihad. The passage underscores the Shia principle that true leadership requires consistency between word and deed, warning that excuses for avoiding duty ultimately lead to the loss of both spiritual and temporal authority.
